annotation.evidence_span: SHOULD NOT issue updates of the Retire Prior To field before receiving RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames that retire all connection IDs indicated by the previous Retire Prior To value.
annotation.interpretation_a: An endpoint can send a new Retire Prior To value as soon as it *believes* all previous connection IDs have been retired, even if it hasn't actually received all the RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames. This relies on the endpoint's internal tracking.
annotation.interpretation_b: An endpoint must wait until it has *definitely* received all RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames corresponding to the previous Retire Prior To value before sending a new one. This requires strict ordering and acknowledgement of frames.
annotation.justification: The use of 'SHOULD NOT' allows for some flexibility, but the core of the sentence hinges on what 'receiving' means. Does it require complete, guaranteed reception, or is a reasonable belief sufficient? This difference in interpretation leads to different implementation choices.
annotation.missing_information: The document does not specify what happens if an endpoint sends a new Retire Prior To value before receiving all the corresponding RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames. Does it cause an error? Is the new value ignored? This missing constraint affects implementation.
